recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if Pharmacy opens a new issue to change the current modeling of professional capacity on MedicationDispense; FHIR-13043 itself is already reflected in the current build.
issue_request: FHIR-13043 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy change request from DSTU2 asking to fix MedicationDispense performer by clarifying that the performer is the dispenser and adding a role back with an appropriate example value set.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied across STU3/R4 workflow-alignment work: a March 2017 QA commit updated MedicationDispense performer/actor wording to say the performer is the dispenser and to note R4 review; the Jira-cited November 2017 workflow-alignment commit 5115fa663f and companion build-fix commit b22fbdaff1 added MedicationDispense.performer.function, bound it to MedicationDispensePerformerFunction, and updated examples. Later source migrations preserved that function/actor model in structuredefinition-MedicationDispense.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-12831 explains the prior removal of the older generic performer.role. The 2017 Zulip thread linked from FHIR-13043 asked that performer explicitly mean dispenser when there was no type. A later 2020 Zulip discussion distinguishes the dispense function from professional capacity, using MedicationDispense.performer.function for what was done and Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or qualifications for pharmacist/physician-type capacity. Later Pharmacy decisions including FHIR-22148 and FHIR-50110 retained and clarified the function/actor model rather than reintroducing the old role element.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. MedicationDispense is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current StructureDefinition already contains MedicationDispense.performer.function with an example binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/medicationdispense-performer-function plus MedicationDispense.performer.actor wording that the actor is the dispenser of the medication.

related_jiras.note: Removed the older generic MedicationDispense.performer.role before FHIR-13043, explaining why the reconciliation should not simply restore that element.
Parallel MedicationAdministration performer issue from the same Zulip discussion; it concerns a different resource and was not decided here.
Later Pharmacy decision retained MedicationDispense.performer.function as example values and adjusted actor/function scope.
Later Pharmacy decision added the current actor comment explaining local restrictions for clinical and non-clinical performer functions.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification request to clarify MedicationDispense performer as dispenser and add a role/function value set.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final seed request that must be compared with current MedicationDispense source.
MedicationDispense source is active in the current core build scope.

evidence_items.summary: MedicationDispense.performer.function exists with example binding to MedicationDispensePerformerFunction and actor says it should be assumed to be the dispenser.
evidence_items.learned: The current source already implements the dispenser clarification and role/function mechanism needed for FHIR-13043.

evidence_items.summary: The Jira-cited workflow alignment and immediate build-fix companion added MedicationDispense.performer.function and its example binding after the earlier role removal.
evidence_items.learned: Historical application explains why the current element is function rather than restoring the old generic role element.

evidence_items.summary: The 2017 linked discussion concluded that without a type, performer should explicitly be documented as the dispenser and reviewed for R4.
evidence_items.learned: This matches the STU3 definition update and explains the issue request.

evidence_items.summary: The 2020 discussion says MedicationDispense.performer.function identifies what was done, while professional capacity such as pharmacist/physician is represented on Practitioner or PractitionerRole.
evidence_items.learned: This supports leaving the current MedicationDispense function value set as a function binding rather than professional-role codes.

evidence_items.summary: Pharmacy voted 6-0-0 to add the current MedicationDispense.performer.actor comment about local restrictions for clinical and non-clinical performer functions.
evidence_items.learned: Later WG action preserved and clarified the function/actor model rather than requiring a new FHIR-13043 edit.
